chapter_theme: Vaalaisami's Njanak Kummi, fourth part: the breath-yoga stated as a sequence (kundalini's vaasi at the root triangle binding the four, the bindu held, the breath subdued at the whirl, Uma's initiation as the first of all yoga), then a Vedantic ladder above bindu (bindu, nada, Shakti, Siva, the Supreme and the sixth, the yoga-sadhaka's waking, the qualityless and partless) and a Vedantic cosmology (five elements, vikshepa, maya; Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat with consciousness above them, the jiva a reflection of Brahman). The part closes with the Siddhars' horse: the breath as a horse of twelve legs, bound with eight ropes, mounted by kundalini's vaasi, which untamed will not enter the whirl's fort, and whose stable is the mind's fort where the enemy knocks.
structure_note: Every stanza ends in the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே or கும்மியடியுங்கடி; the reading is what the stanza adds. The part runs from practice (2593 to 2597) through the states above bindu (2598 to 2602), the breath and the whirl (2603 to 2604), the karmas and the triad of pasu, pasam and pati (2605 to 2608), the Vedantic cosmos and the reflection (2609 to 2611), and the horse of the vaasi (2612 to 2617), which the next part continues with the thirteen enemies.

2593.reading: What is to be kindled? At the root of the triangle in the circle, by kundalini's vaasi one establishes fullness and binds the four; is this not the knowing, girl of knowledge?
2593.nuance: திரிகோணவட்ட மூலம், the triangle in the circle at the root, is the muladhara as tradition draws it. வாகியினால் is read as வாசியினால், matching 2615; the four that are bound are not named (2615 binds the eight and the four). நியாபம் is unclear, perhaps ஞாபகம் (knowing) or நியாயம் (the right way).

2594.reading: Hold the bindu bound and do not push it out; subdue the breath at the whirl without struggling; do not struggle with the pointing mind; throw off the sloth of lust.
2594.nuance: Three restraints and one dismissal: seed, breath and mind are held, and desire is called sloth (காமச் சோம்பல்), which 2595 then pairs with sleep. சுழிக்காற்று, the whirl-breath, is the breath at the suzhumunai.

2595.reading: Sloth and sleep must not be; do not take on food-craving and grief; standing in the gaze on Samba Sadasiva, join and dance the kummi.
2595.nuance: அன்ன சுதி is unclear: perhaps அன்ன ருசி (taste for food) or அன்ன சுத்தி (purity of food). The stanza turns the negatives of 2594 into the single positive, the fixed gaze (நாட்டம்) on Sadasiva.

2596.reading: The sixty-four arts come to hand and the kalpa of knowledge comes and merges; the good siddhas and the freed said that such a one is a god.
2596.nuance: சஷ்டிவித்தை is the சதுஷ்ஷஷ்டி கலை, the sixty-four arts. ஞானக் கற்பம் uses the medical word kalpa for knowledge itself, the rejuvenation that is knowing; 2607 calls this kalpa the true one. The deifying of the adept is credited to the siddhas and muktas, not claimed by the poet.

2597.reading: Uma's initiation is the first for yoga, the first initiation for every yoga; do not abandon enjoyment; seek the worship of Shakti.
2597.nuance: போகம் (enjoyment) is the word that carries the stanza. Taken plainly it tells the practitioner not to renounce the body's pleasure; in the Shakta reading of tradition it is the enjoyment of the goddess in the body that the yoga makes possible. Either way Shakti's initiation precedes every other yoga.

2598.reading: Seek them: bindu, the ancient nada, Shakti, Siva who abides with her, and the Supreme; crossing these, the sixfold way is the yoga-practitioner's waking.
2598.nuance: Five are named (விந்து, நாதம், சத்தி, சிவம், பரம்) and the stanza says six (வகையாறு); the sixth may be the waking (சாக்கிரம்) itself or an unnamed term. சாதக சாக்கிரம், the practitioner's waking, is the first of a set of yogic states that 2599 and 2601 continue; it is a 'waking' above the ordinary waking, as in the Tirumanthiram's avasthas within avasthas.

2599.reading: That waking is the sphere above bindu; reaching it is the qualityless, the partless; if one looks, it is the stainless state without support; if one does not look at it, that is the end.
2599.nuance: நிர்க்குண நிஷ்களம் are Vedantic and Agamic names for the Supreme without attributes or parts. நிராதாராமலம் is read as நிராதார அமலம், the supportless stainless, that is, above the six adharas. அந்தம் at the close may be 'the end' as goal or as death; 2600 takes it up as a name for the state.

2600.reading: That is the end, girl; who, having seen these six above, knows the way of knowledge? See the great ones whose minds are discerning, serve them, and dance.
2600.nuance: The ladder of 2598 and 2599 is declared unknowable from the text alone; the stanza sends the hearer to the living great (பெரியோர்), the kummi's usual name for the guru.

2601.reading: Serving is the twilight rite of austerity; standing as yoga is bindu and nada; the Sadasiva-waking that agrees with the life-breath is that very place.
2601.nuance: The stanza pairs three terms with three definitions: service with sandhya (தவ சந்தி), yoga with bindu-nada, and the Sadasiva-waking with the breath or soul (ஆவி). சதாசிவ சாக்கிரம் is a yogic state above the practitioner's waking of 2598; the names of the Siva-avasthas in 2685 to 2689 belong to the same scheme.

2602.reading: Letting go 'a', letting go 'u', with the trace in the upper whirl, leaving fire by means of air, letting go 'ma', see the inner substance of nada and bindu, praise it and dance.
2602.nuance: அ, உ, ம are the three letters of Om; the stanza releases them one by one and places what remains in the upper whirl (மேற்சுழி). அங்கியை விட்டுக் காலாலே is read as leaving the fire (the heat at the root) by the air (the breath); in cipher fire and air are also the right and left breaths. The 'inner substance' is what is left of Om when its letters are gone.

2603.reading: What is the roaring? Prana and apana; kindling them in samadhi, the out-breath makes it shine, and the sun's radiance is the brightness; seek it and dance.
2603.nuance: முழக்கம் (roar) is the sound of the breath or of nada. இரேசகம் is the rechaka, the out-breath, and இரவி காந்தி the sun's light, in cipher the right breath or the inner fire; the word order is loose and the sentence may divide otherwise.

2604.reading: Those who look do not see the suzhumunai; they do not know that it is the tip of the nose; turning back the road, see the great ones, praise them and dance.
2604.nuance: The kummi places the suzhumunai at the nose-tip (மூக்கு நுனி), the point of the yogic nasikagra gaze, where most Siddhar texts place the whirl at the brow or the crown; the difference may be of the opening rather than the channel. மார்க்கம் மறித்து, turning the road back, is read of the breath's outward road, as in 2616.

2605.reading: Praise, girl, the gathered store; change deeds into fullness, girl; cast away the coming and the accumulated karma; destroy what is to be destroyed, and dance.
2605.nuance: ஆகாமியம் and சஞ்சிதம் are two of the three karmas of Vedanta, the deeds yet to come and the stored deeds; the third, the deeds now ripening (பிராரத்தம்), may be the சேகரம் (store) of the first line. The stanza's cure for karma is to turn it into பூரணம், the fullness that 2639 says the ignorant merely name.

2606.reading: The place without bond is the sky-going; standing in one half is yoga; for those without a country it is the Brahma-knowledge samadhi, and it is the twofold spreading.
2606.nuance: கேசம் is read as கேசரம் (khechara, the sky-going state), as in 2642 and 2657. ஒரு பாதி, one half, may be the moon's half or one of the two breaths. விருவிசர்ப்பம் is obscure, perhaps இரு விசர்ப்பம், a twofold spreading. A short reading is that bondlessness, yoga and samadhi are three names for one state.

2607.reading: This kalpa is the true one, girl; all other desires are very small; join the silence of Sadasiva, the bliss of the Supreme, and dance.
2607.nuance: The kalpa (கற்பம்) here is the knowledge-kalpa of 2596, not a drug; it is set against காமம், all other wanting, which is அற்பம் (petty). The goal is named as silence and bliss together.

2608.reading: Call the bond the body and that bound soul the life; what stands in love is what they call fixity in Brahman.
2608.nuance: Saiva Siddhanta's triad is recast: pasam is the body, pasu the soul, and in place of pati stands நேசம், love, as the state of Brahma-nishta. The attribution என்பார் (they say) keeps it as a received definition. 2662 will tell the hearer to drop pati and pasam altogether.

2609.reading: The beginning of the body is the five elements; the beginning of the other, of action, is projection; the beginning of delusion is maya; hear all of it, girl.
2609.nuance: விட்சேபம் (vikshepa) is the Vedantic projecting power of ignorance, paired with concealment (ஆவரணம்); the stanza assigns it to activity and maya to delusion (மோகம்). The three 'beginnings' (ஆதி) are a compressed Vedantic account of body, act and mind.

2610.reading: Above the Avyakrita who holds the eggs, above Hiranyagarbha who is Vishnu, above the lightning-bright Virat Purusha, above these there is consciousness.
2610.nuance: வியாகிருதன், இரணியகர்ப்பன் and விராட் புருடன் are the three cosmic selves of Vedanta, presiding over the universe's deep sleep, dream and waking; the kummi equates Hiranyagarbha with Vishnu. இண்டமுண்ட is garbled, perhaps அண்டமுண்ட (who swallowed the eggs). சைதன்னியம் (chaitanya), consciousness, is above all three and is named Brahman in 2611.

2611.reading: The conscious substance itself is Brahman, girl; for that witness, what comes after is the reflection; by pure knowledge that stands true, the reflection can be cast off.
2611.nuance: பிம்பம் and பிரதிபிம்பம் are the Vedantic image and reflection: Brahman as the witness (சாட்சி) and the jiva as its reflection in the mind. உபிந்தி is unclear, perhaps உபாதி (the adjunct, as in chapter 141). The stanza says the reflection is discarded, not the witness.

2612.reading: Yes, girl, if this state is seen, you yourself are the beginning and the end; for us, by the horse of the vaasi, there is the greatly good way, girl.
2612.nuance: The first half is the Vedantic conclusion of 2610 and 2611: the hearer is herself first and last. The second half introduces the கற்றிரை (horse) that fills the rest of the part, the breath as a mount rather than a thing held.

2613.reading: The horse of good breed has great speed and stands above the life that is its load; if one gives it a course street by street, one can watch the horse's show.
2613.nuance: சாதிக் குதிரை is a thoroughbred; in the cipher the horse is the breath, as 2612 has just said. சருதாருயிர் is garbled; the sense taken is that the breath rides above the life it carries. வீதிக்கு வீதி, street to street, is read as the breath's course through the channels, which 2627 names as streets.

2614.reading: That axle-level cannot be bound, since its legs are twelve; but if one ties it with eight ropes, it comes under measure.
2614.nuance: The numbers carry the stanza. கால் is both leg and wind: the twelve legs match the twelve finger-breadths that tradition gives as the breath's reach, and the Tirumanthiram's horse of twelve legs. The eight ropes are taken as the eight limbs of yoga, or the eight that 2615 binds with the four. அச்சு மட்டம், the axle's level, is obscure.

2615.reading: Will it be bound? At the gate of impurity, in the middle of the centre, by kundalini's vaasi, if one binds the eight and the four and reveres them, one can mount and ride.
2615.nuance: மலவாயில், the gate of impurity, is the body's lowest opening, so the centre is the muladhara of 2593. The eight and the four are not explained; tradition offers the eight petals and four petals of the lower lotuses, or the eight siddhis and four steps. The horse is bound where kundalini sleeps and ridden from there.

2616.reading: Without taming the subtle horse one cannot go inside the fort of the whirl; the breath walks ahead for a thousand kadham.
2616.nuance: சுழிக் கோடு, the whirl's fort or horn, is the suzhumunai as an enclosure to be entered. The last line is the plainest statement in the part of why the breath must be tamed: left alone it runs outward an immense distance (a kadham is some ten miles), that is, it is spent on the world.

2617.reading: In the stable where the horse is tied, in the fort of the mind, in the market street, the enemy himself comes and knocks; ask what that is, girl.
2617.nuance: The mind is at once stable, fort and bazaar; the enemy who knocks is not named here but in the next part, where Kama and twelve kin are counted. சந்தைப்பேட்டை, the market quarter, makes the mind a place of trade as well as defence.

links.note: Tirumular lists Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita as the presiding selves under the 'that' of the great saying; Vaalaisami stacks the same three with consciousness above them, and chapter 141 will assign them to the Supreme's waking, dream and sleep.

Tirumular maps 'thou', 'that' and 'art' onto pasu, pati and sayujya, keeping the Siddhanta triad whole. Vaalaisami redefines the same triad from the Vedanta side: pasam the body, pasu the soul, and love standing where pati stood. Same three words, two systems of reference.

Both make the breath a horse with twelve legs (ஈராறு கால் and காலோ பன்னிரண்டு), legs being winds, and both say it must be tied fast; Tirumular promises long life from the binding, the kummi only that the horse comes under measure.

Tirumular's two horses come under control only by the guru's grace, since no one knows the skill to catch them; Vaalaisami gives the technique, binding at the lowest gate by kundalini's vaasi, and sends the hearer to the great ones elsewhere (2600, 2604) rather than here.
The enemy knocking at the mind's fort is unnamed here; the next part opens by naming him Kama, eldest of all, and counts his brothers, children and friends to thirteen.

source_issues: 2593: வாகியினால் is probably a misprint for வாசியினால் (so 2615); நியாபம் is unclear.
2599: the line ends with a stray comma after the refrain; so 2613 and 2614.
2607: சார்ர் is a doubled letter for சார்.
2610: இண்டமுண்ட and மிண்ணு are garbled; the sense is supplied from the Vedantic names.
2614: the refrain is followed by a stray space and comma.
